title: [12/1/2023] Teaching hours per year by each teacher in 2001
prompt: The graph below shows the hours of teaching per year done by each teacher in four different countries in 2001. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart illustrates the number of teaching hours per year for teachers at three different educational levels in four countries in 2001.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, teachers in the USA spent the most time teaching across all educational levels compared to the other three nations. Additionally, in Spain, upper secondary teachers had notably higher teaching hours than their primary and lower secondary counterparts, while the differences between levels in other countries were relatively modest.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the USA and Spain, American teachers' annual teaching hours varied significantly, with a gap of around 270 hours between the lowest at primary level (830 hours) and the highest at upper secondary level (1100 hours), while lower secondary educators taught for 1080 hours. In Spain, while primary and lower secondary teachers spent about 600 hours teaching, their upper secondary colleagues worked substantially more, at nearly 980 hours per year.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining countries, Japanese teachers across all three levels had relatively similar teaching loads, ranging from 600 to 680 hours annually. Similarly, in Iceland, primary teachers spent approximately 600 hours teaching, though their secondary counterparts worked longer hours, at around 800 hours per year.
